1474-the-illustrious-gaudissart.creator: Honore De Balzac
1474-the-illustrious-gaudissart.description: A book by Honore De Balzac. ly he is neither Parisian nor provincial,--he is a traveller. He sees nothing to the core: men and places he knows by their names; as for things, he looks merely at their surface, and he has his own little tape-line with which to measure them. His glance shoots over all things and penetrates none. He occupies himself with a great deal, yet nothing occupies him.

arxiv-1701-00559.creator: Zi-Wu Wang, Yao Xiao, Wei-Ping Li, Run-Ze Li, Zhi-Qing Li

arxiv-1706-02110.title: Material Budget Calculation of the new Inner Tracking System, ALICE
arxiv-1706-02110.creator: WANCHALOEM POONSAWAT, CHINORAT KOBDAJ, MARIO SITTA, YUPENG YAN
arxiv-1706-02110.description: Abstract The ALICE Collaboration aims at studying the physics of strongly interacting matter by building up a dedicated heavy-ion detector. The Inner Tracking System (ITS) is located in the heart of the ALICE Detector surrounding the interaction point. Now, ALICE has a plan to upgrade the inner tracking system for rare probes at low transverse momentum.

arxiv-2011-01108.title: End-to-end anti-spoofing with RawNet2
arxiv-2011-01108.creator: Hemlata Tak 1 , Jose Patino 1 , Massimiliano Todisco 1 , Andreas Nautsch 1 Nicholas Evans 1 and Anthony Larcher 2
arxiv-2011-01108.description: Abstract Spoofing countermeasures aim to protect automatic speaker verification systems from attempts to manipulate their reliability with the use of spoofed speech signals. While results from the most recent ASVspoof 2019 evaluation show great potential to detect most forms of attack, some continue to evade detection. This paper reports the first application of RawNet2 to anti-spoofing.

arxiv-2312-16801.title: Sum of squares decomposition of positive polynomials with rational coefficients
arxiv-2312-16801.creator: Santiago Laplagne
arxiv-2312-16801.description: Abstract . We present an example of a strictly positive polynomial with rational coefficients that can be decomposed as a sum of squares of polynomials over ℝ {\mathbb{R}} but not over ℚ {\mathbb{Q}} . This answers an open question by C. Scheiderer posed as the second question in [ 14 , Section 5.1] .

arxiv-2504-18013.title: Regularity for Hamiltonian stationary equations in ℝ n ≤ 4 n \mathbb{R}_{n\leq 4}^{n}
arxiv-2504-18013.creator: Arunima Bhattacharya
arxiv-2504-18013.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arunima Bhattacharya. In this paper, we study the regularity of solutions to the Hamiltonian stationary equation in complex Euclidean space. We show that in dimensions n ≤ 4 n\leq 4 , for all values of the Lagrangian phase, any C 1 , 1 C^{1,1} solution is smooth and derive a C k , α C^{k,\alpha} estimate for it, where k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 .

arxiv-2506-02243.title: From Features to Structure: Task-Aware Graph Construction for Relational and Tabular Learning with GNNs
arxiv-2506-02243.creator: Tamara Cucumides, Floris Geerts
arxiv-2506-02243.description: Abstract . Tabular and relational data remain the most ubiquitous formats in real-world machine learning applications, spanning domains from finance to healthcare. Although both formats offer structured representations, they pose distinct challenges for modern deep learning methods, which typically assume flat, feature-aligned inputs.

arxiv-2506-10389.title: EQA-RM : A Generative Embodied Reward Model with Test-time Scaling
arxiv-2506-10389.creator: Yuhang Chen, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen
arxiv-2506-10389.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuhang Chen, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen. Reward Models (RMs), vital for large model alignment, are underexplored for complex embodied tasks like Embodied Question Answering (EQA) where nuanced evaluation of agents’ spatial, temporal, and logical understanding is critical yet not considerred by generic approaches. We introduce EQA-RM , a novel generative multimodal reward model specifically architected for EQA, trained via our innovative Contrastive Group Relative Policy Optimization ( C-GRPO ) strategy to learn fine-grained behavioral distinctions.

arxiv-2507-04543.title: Context-sensitive norm enforcement reduces sanctioning costs in spatial public goods games Journal: Applied Mathematics and Computation
arxiv-2507-04543.creator: Hsuan-Wei Lee, Colin Cleveland, and Attila Szolnoki
arxiv-2507-04543.description: Abstract Uniform punishment policies can sustain cooperation in social dilemmas but impose severe costs on enforcers, creating a second-order free-rider problem that undermines the very mechanism designed to prevent exploitation. We show that the remedy is not a harsher stick but a smarter one.

pmc-10739001.title: SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN PHYSICAL AND OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY HOME HEALTH CARE VISITS FOR PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA
pmc-10739001.creator: Ashwath Muruganand, Rebecca Lassell, Shih-Yin Lin, Kimberly Convery, Jason Fletcher, Abraham Brody
pmc-10739001.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). People living with Dementia (PLWD) utilize Home Health Care (HHC) services such as Physical Therapy (PT) and Occupational Therapy (OT), but little is known about service utilization patterns among PLWD from different socioeconomic backgrounds. We aimed to identify disparities in service utilization in PLWD in a HHC setting across socioeconomic backgrounds using a measure of geographic socioeconomic deprivation, the Area Deprivation Index (ADI). ADI is a composite measure of census variables describing socioeconomic disadvantage, reported as national percentile rank.

pmc-11341898.title: Mutant huntingtin impairs neurodevelopment in human brain organoids through CHCHD2-mediated neurometabolic failure
pmc-11341898.creator: Pawel Lisowski, Selene Lickfett, Agnieszka Rybak-Wolf, Carmen Menacho, Stephanie Le, Tancredi Massimo Pentimalli, Sofia Notopoulou, Werner Dykstra, Daniel Oehler, Sandra López-Calcerrada, Barbara Mlody, Maximilian Otto, Haijia Wu, Yasmin Richter, Philipp Roth, Ruchika Anand, Linda A. M. Kulka, David
pmc-11341898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Expansion of the glutamine tract (poly-Q) in the protein huntingtin (HTT) causes the neurodegenerative disorder Huntington’s disease (HD). Emerging evidence suggests that mutant HTT (mHTT) disrupts brain development. To gain mechanistic insights into the neurodevelopmental impact of human mHTT, we engineered male induced pluripotent stem cells to introduce a biallelic or monoallelic mutant 70Q expansion or to remove the poly-Q tract of HTT. The introduction of a 70Q mutation caused aberrant development of cerebral organoids with loss of neural progenitor organization.

pmc-11611926.title: Technological Remedies for Social Problems: Defining and Demarcating Techno-Fixes and Techno-Solutionism
pmc-11611926.creator: Henrik Skaug Sætra, Evan Selinger
pmc-11611926.description: Can technology resolve social problems by reducing them to engineering challenges? In the 1960s, Alvin Weinberg answered yes, popularizing the term “techno-fix” in the process. The concept was immediately criticized and over time evolved into a disparaging term—a synonym for unrealistic technological proposals and their advocates. As the debate progressed, skepticism grew to include condemnation of a related term: “techno-solutionism.

pmc-12385729.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Early Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury in Neurocritical Care: A Comparative Analysis of XGBoost, GBM, and Random Forest Algorithms
pmc-12385729.creator: Keun Soo Kim, Tae Jin Yoon, Joonghyun Ahn, Jeong-Am Ryu
pmc-12385729.description: Background: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a pivotal concern in neurocritical care, impacting patient survival and quality of life. This study harnesses machine learning (ML) techniques to predict the occurrence of AKI in patients receiving hyperosmolar therapy, aiming to optimize patient outcomes in neurocritical settings.

pmc-12535034.creator: Noriko Kubota, Reo Sueno, Yosai Mori, Kazunori Miyata, Tomoyuki Kunishige, Yuji Nakano, Hitoshi Goto, Fumiki Okamoto
pmc-12535034.description: PurposeTo evaluate clinical and optical coherence tomography (OCT) findings and visual outcomes in patients with macular pseudohole (MPH), epiretinal membrane foveoschisis (ERM-FS), and lamellar macular hole (LMH) based on axial length (AL).MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients diagnosed with MPH, ERM-FS, and LMH who underwent vitrectomy and were followed for at least 6 months postoperatively.

pmc-12540984.title: MDM2 promotes CELF6 ubiquitination-dependent degradation to promote neuroblastoma cell proliferation
pmc-12540984.creator: Zhenzhen Zhao, Bao Zhang, Xu Zhang, Changchun Li
pmc-12540984.description: The ubiquitin–proteasome system plays a crucial role in neuroblastoma progression, yet the regulation of key degradation targets remains incompletely understood. By integrating transcriptomic and proteomic data, we identified nine candidate proteins, including CELF6, whose degradation is potentially mediated by ubiquitination. Survival analyses revealed that high CELF6 expression correlated with a favorable prognosis.

pmc-13028218.title: Current Trends and Future Prospects of Radiomics and Machine Learning (ML) Models in Spinal Tumors—A Narrative Review
pmc-13028218.creator: Vivek Sanker, Suhrud Panchawgh, Anmol Kaur, Vinay Suresh, Dhanya Mahesh, Eeman Ahmad, Srinath Hariharan, Dhiraj Pangal, Maria Jose Cavgnaro, Mirabela Rusu, John Ratliff, Atman Desai
pmc-13028218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The intersection between radiomics, the computational analysis of imaging data, and machine learning (ML) may lead to new developments in the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of diseases. For spinal tumors specifically, applications of these fields appear promising. In this educational narrative review, we provide a summary of the current advancements in radiomics and artificial intelligence (AI), as well as applications of both fields in the diagnosis and management of spinal tumors.

Introduction

Tongue fasciculations, with electrophysiologically confirmed denervation, strongly support a diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in bulbar presentations, although mimics have been reported [1]. While “tongue tremor” or rhythmic movements have been described in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) [2, 3], genuine fasciculations with electrophysiologically confirmed denervation are not expected.
